method: steps: modules (Make) or nodes (n8n) on the accepted path from trigger to webhook response, counted from the committed blueprint and workflow JSON; the Make router counts as a module.

failureHandling: branches the platform itself evaluates (Make router routes with filters, n8n If nodes and Respond outcomes); exception typing comes from period.exception.code returned by the client endpoint.
recovery: modules or nodes on the retry route and whether the replay reuses period.retry.sameIdempotencyKey.

duplicateEffects: simulated lost reply through src/client-endpoint.mjs with the synthetic export fixtures: the same request evaluated twice and the accepted hand-off posted twice; counts extra acceptance effects plus extra hand-off deliveries.

direct: the same accepted, retry and changed-schema periods posted straight to src/client-endpoint.mjs with no workflow platform (scripts/direct-baseline.mjs); steps and retry steps are endpoint calls; measured by local simulation.
Computed by scripts/compute-comparison.mjs; no live Make or n8n run is claimed.

native.steps: 4: project permitted capture, bind the exchange-supplied termsVersion, build job contract, run acceptance
native.failureHandling: typed exception per period: ingestion_missing, ingestion_not_permitted, capture_stale, schema_changed, terms_changed, token_used_as_task_ref, follow_up_not_new_task
native.recovery: replay with the same idempotencyKey (request digest) returns the original committed result; uncommitted first request fabricates nothing
native.source: vendored PR 684 recurring-journey COMPARISON_ROWS.native (repo and sha in vendor/PINS.json)

make.steps: 7 modules on the accepted path (11 in the scenario): Receive Period Capture > Shape Capture Fields > Period Record JSON > Evaluate Period > Route On Period > Post Accepted Output > Respond Accepted
make.failureHandling: 3 router routes with filters (Accepted, Retryable, Not retryable); typed period.exception.code from the SameDayDesk client endpoint (same vendored journey as native)
make.recovery: 3 modules on the retry route (Wait Before Replay > Replay Same Key > Respond Replayed); replay reuses period.retry.sameIdempotencyKey: true
make.duplicateEffects: 0: 2 evaluations gave 1 acceptance effect (replay recovered true, secondEffect false); 2 hand-off posts gave 1 delivery

n8n.steps: 7 nodes on the accepted path (15 in the workflow, 3 of them the separate FlowAssert branch): Receive Period Capture > Kit Settings > Shape Capture Fields > Evaluate Period > Accepted? > Post Accepted Output > Respond Accepted
n8n.failureHandling: 2 If nodes (Accepted?, Retryable?) and 3 response outcomes (Respond Accepted 200, Respond Replayed 202, Respond Exception 422); typed period.exception.code from the SameDayDesk client endpoint (same vendored journey as native)
n8n.recovery: 3 nodes on the retry route (Wait Before Replay > Replay Same Key > Respond Replayed); replay reuses period.retry.sameIdempotencyKey: true
n8n.duplicateEffects: 0: 2 evaluations gave 1 acceptance effect (replay recovered true, secondEffect false); 2 hand-off posts gave 1 delivery

direct.steps: 2 calls on the accepted path: POST /periods > POST /periods/accepted
direct.failureHandling: 0 platform branches; the caller reads period.exception.code and period.retry.retryable (capture_stale retryable true, uncommitted retryable true, continuation_file_missing retryable false, schema_changed retryable false); typed period.exception.code from the SameDayDesk client endpoint (same vendored journey as native)
direct.recovery: 1 call on the retry route (POST /periods with Idempotency-Key = period.retry.sameIdempotencyKey); replay recovered true, secondEffect false; uncommitted then committed on the same key true; changed schema recovered by the declared adapter later-period-output-keys.v1 on a new key
direct.duplicateEffects: 0: 11 calls over 2 accepted keys gave 2 acceptance effects and 2 deliveries
direct.source: measured by local simulation: scripts/direct-baseline.mjs posts to src/client-endpoint.mjs with no workflow platform; synthetic fixtures; not a live run

nativeVsDirect: Native row: vendored PR 684 recurring-journey COMPARISON_ROWS.native, unchanged (repo and sha in vendor/PINS.json).
Both kits reach the same period.* as native because the client endpoint runs the same vendored journey; the platform adds trigger, shaping, routing and hand-off steps around it.

Duplicate-effect protection comes from the request-digest idempotency key enforced by the client endpoint, not from Make or n8n. A platform-level retry that bypasses the endpoint would not be deduplicated by the platform.

Direct row: a caller posting to the client endpoint itself needs 2 calls on the accepted path and 1 on the retry route, with 0 duplicate effects; the platforms add trigger, shaping, routing and response steps around the same endpoint.
Counts are from committed JSON and a local simulation, not from a live Make or n8n execution.
